# Opal Pettigrew

## Overview

- **Gender:** Female  <sub>[v1 c15 P28](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0028)</sub>
- **Status:** Deceased  <sub>[v3 c14 P30](../source/v03-c14.md#nw-v03-c14-p0030)</sub>
- **Role:** Schoolteacher  <sub>[v2 c19 P60](../source/v02-c19.md#nw-v02-c19-p0060), [v3 c11 P6](../source/v03-c11.md#nw-v03-c11-p0006)</sub>

## Appearance

Opal Pettigrew was an attractive girl with a radiant complexion, vivid blue eyes, and long, yellow hair that she wore in braids or styled up. As a child, her hair was styled in a long blonde plait, and she was noted by others for her striking, full-figured appearance. Towards the end of her life, she became frail, thin, and pale, with a feverish flush on her cheeks and hands that appeared almost transparent.

_Sources: [v1 c15 P28](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0028), [v1 c28 P3](../source/v01-c28.md#nw-v01-c28-p0003), [v1 c30 P43](../source/v01-c30.md#nw-v01-c30-p0043), [v1 c35 P1](../source/v01-c35.md#nw-v01-c35-p0001), [v3 c11 P4](../source/v03-c11.md#nw-v03-c11-p0004), [v3 c14 P2](../source/v03-c14.md#nw-v03-c14-p0002), [v3 c14 P5](../source/v03-c14.md#nw-v03-c14-p0005)_

## Personality

Opal had a sunny, cheerful disposition and enjoyed the fun, gay aspects of life, though she was deeply preoccupied with young men, romance, and compliments. She possessed a dramatic, superstitious side and was prone to fits of hysterics when frightened or overwhelmed. Though she often behaved in a lighthearted or sentimental manner, she felt a profound terror of dying when confronted with her fatal illness. In her final days, she showed a childlike desire for companionship and affection.

_Sources: [v1 c16 P18](../source/v01-c16.md#nw-v01-c16-p0018), [v1 c23 P16](../source/v01-c23.md#nw-v01-c23-p0016), [v1 c26 P6](../source/v01-c26.md#nw-v01-c26-p0006), [v1 c26 P21](../source/v01-c26.md#nw-v01-c26-p0021), [v1 c28 P1](../source/v01-c28.md#nw-v01-c28-p0001), [v1 c35 P1](../source/v01-c35.md#nw-v01-c35-p0001), [v2 c26 P59](../source/v02-c26.md#nw-v02-c26-p0059), [v3 c14 P11](../source/v03-c14.md#nw-v03-c14-p0011), [v3 c14 P17](../source/v03-c14.md#nw-v03-c14-p0017)_

## History

Opal Pettigrew grew up in Brierley and attended the local school, where she shared an aisle with Nell Harcourt and was part of the school's social circle. She joined Nell and Isolde in forming a tale-writing society, participated in games like acting out Elaine, and entered the Regent's class under Miss Thorne. After studying at the Academy in Regent's, she earned her teacher's license and took up a teaching position at the Delford school. Throughout her youth, she engaged in numerous flirtations and acquired many suitors, including Nelson Atkins, Wilbur Blair, Leonard Kimball, Varley Bell, and Herb Tranter. During the winter of her teaching years, she contracted a severe bout of congestion that developed into galloping consumption. Though she initially concealed her illness and insisted she would resume teaching, she steadily weakened and was forced to give up her work. She spent her final summer at home in Brierley, sharing poignant conversations about life and death with Nell. Opal passed away peacefully in her sleep shortly thereafter, and was buried in the Brierley church cemetery.

## Quotes

> Farewell, sweet sister  <sub>[v1 c28 P16](../source/v01-c28.md#nw-v01-c28-p0016)</sub>

> Me! Well, I am completely fine. Never in my entire existence have I felt superior to this. To be sure, I was somewhat weakened by that congestion during the previous winter. However, simply look at my complexion. Surely, I do not appear at all like a sick person.  <sub>[v3 c11 P57](../source/v03-c11.md#nw-v03-c11-p0057)</sub>

> Nell, the time is drawing near when I will be resting in that place. You, Isolde, and everyone else will be moving around, brimming with vitality—while I will be situated there—within the ancient cemetery—deceased!  <sub>[v3 c14 P7](../source/v03-c14.md#nw-v03-c14-p0007)</sub>

> And, oh, Nell—dying is not what I want. The thought of dying frightens me.  <sub>[v3 c14 P11](../source/v03-c14.md#nw-v03-c14-p0011)</sub>

> I want to live. I want to live the way other girls do. I—I desire to get married, Nell—and—and—possess tiny children. You are aware that babies were always something I loved, Nell. To nobody else except you could I admit this. That you comprehend, I know. Furthermore, poor Herb—he—he cares for me and my love belongs to him, Nell. Nothing was meant to me by the others, yet he matters—and provided I could remain alive, I would become his wife and experience such happiness. Oh, Nell, this is difficult.  <sub>[v3 c14 P17](../source/v03-c14.md#nw-v03-c14-p0017)</sub>
